section_text: Regulatory compliance for the weather-monitoring cubesat requires national licensing (FCC/NOAA for US launches), ITU frequency coordination, export control compliance (ITAR/EAR), debris mitigation plan approval, and launch range safety certification. Key filings include FCC Space Station License (26-week lead time), ITU Frequency Notification (18 weeks), Debris Mitigation Plan (12 weeks), and Launch Range Safety certification (8 weeks). For non-US launches, equivalent national space agency authorization is required. Export controls apply to hardware and software transfers, requiring EAR/ITAR compliance reviews. The satellite must comply with orbital debris mitigation standards, demonstrating post-mission disposal within 25 years. Spectrum coordination must be completed 4-5 months before launch, and ground station licensing requires separate national telecommunications authority approval. Insurance requirements typically include third-party liability coverage of $100M-$500M.
assumptions: US-based launch requiring FCC licensing and NOAA coordination for weather data
S-band communications requiring ITU frequency coordination
International suppliers requiring export control compliance
LEO orbit at 600-800 km altitude with passive deorbit capability
Commercial launch provider with established range safety requirements
Weather data sharing agreements may be required depending on data resolution

prioritized_checklist.task: Submit FCC Space Station License application
Submit debris mitigation plan for approval

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Frequency interference issues with other operators
Export control violations during international shipping
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Early legal review and proper documentation
